thesis: A deleveraging managed-care and PBM franchise with ROIC rising to 13.4% and a 12.29% FCF yield trades below its own 5-year minimum P/E, EV/EBITDA and P/FCF, where the price implies a -16% revenue decline that reaffirmed guidance does not support.
reason: Every cash-flow multiple is below its 5-year floor, and returns, leverage and buybacks are all improving, so the downside is cushioned by cash yield. PBM-reform risk and a 2.3% net margin cap conviction at 4, not 5. A 7% position takes Healthcare to about 14% alongside ZTS, well within the 30% cap, and cash covers it.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 9%, giving up the five-year improvement from 8.8% to 13.4%.
TTM operating margin falls below 3.5%, under the FY2025 five-year low of 3.7%, showing PBM reform or medical-cost pressure is compressing profitability structurally.
TTM net margin falls below 1.5%, near the FY2024 trough of 1.4%, confirming margin compression is structural.
TTM FCF margin falls below 2.5%, under the five-year low of 3.1%, signalling earnings quality and buyback capacity are deteriorating.
